name: TeamStarWolf - Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days (September and October 2026) Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques bound in the case study of the Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway zero-days of September and October 2026 (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-88779). No source names ATT&CK ids, so every binding is the study's own. Score 75: a vendor bulletin, CVE record or government advisory describes the behavior. Score 50: a security vendor's report describes it. Score 25: a capability or a close-but-inexact fit. Comments carry the study's source numbers.

legendItems.label: 75: described in a vendor bulletin, CVE record or government advisory
50: described in a security vendor's report
25: capability or inexact fit, labelled in the comment

metadata.value: 75 = vendor bulletin, CVE record or government advisory; 50 = security vendor's report; 25 = capability or inexact fit. No severity, prevalence or coverage is measured.

techniques.comment: Version fingerprinting of more than 100 systems on 21 and 22 Aug 2026 (Unit 42); wide-scale scanning after the public proof of concept on 29 Sep 2026. Sources: [26] [45].
Custom WHIPSHOT PHP web shell and SLAPSHOT Python tunneler (GTIG and Mandiant, 29 Sep 2026). Sources: [25].

Exploits of CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 against unmitigated NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances (Citrix CTX697096 and KEV, 27 Sep 2026); activity from early Sep 2026. Sources: [1] [11] [13] [25].
Root shell in the playbook GreyNoise saw on 24 Sep 2026; command-injection web shell on 21 Sep 2026 (Unit 42). Sources: [26] [28].
Capability: SLAPSHOT is described as a Python tunneler; no interpreter run is described (GTIG, 29 Sep 2026). Sources: [25].
DTLS web shells 4 to 24 Sep 2026, a three-stage web shell on 21 Sep, a web shell at a Rapid7 victim on 24 Sep, and WHIPSHOT. Sources: [25] [26] [27] [49].
Hidden PHP web shell behind a fake stylesheet path (GreyNoise, 24 Sep 2026). Sources: [28].
Files staged on appliances 4 to 24 Sep 2026 (Unit 42); crafted SAML usernames carrying download attempts (2 Oct 2026, press). Sources: [26] [34].
WHIPSHOT hides command and control in native HTTP headers (GTIG, 29 Sep 2026). Sources: [25].
Actor tunnelled in through SLAPSHOT for manual internal reconnaissance (GTIG, 29 Sep 2026). Sources: [25].
Appliance configuration exposing encrypted admin passwords and LDAP, RADIUS and TACACS bind secrets (Rapid7, 28 Sep 2026); credential harvesting (GTIG). Sources: [25] [27].
TLS private keys in the staged appliance configuration (Rapid7, 28 Sep 2026). Sources: [27].
Appliance configuration staged for unauthenticated retrieval (Rapid7, 28 Sep 2026). Sources: [27].
Access-log scrubbing; bound at the parent because the logs are web-server logs (GTIG, 29 Sep 2026). Sources: [25].
CVE-2026-88779 crashes the SAML service and forces reboots (2 to 4 Oct 2026); KEV DoS entry 4 Oct; CISA on reboot as an accelerator for CVE-2026-88771 (9 Oct 2026). Sources: [11] [13] [27] [34].
